Then the Adversary answered the Lord, saying, “Has Job feared God for nothing?
Have You not made a hedge around him, around his household, and around all that he has on every side? You have blessed the work of his hands, and his possessions have increased in the land.
But stretch out Your hand now, and touch all that he has, and he will curse You to Your face.”
The Lord said to the Adversary, “Behold, all that he has is in your power; only do not stretch out your hand against his person.”
So a day came when his sons and his daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother’s house,
and a messenger came to Job and said, “The oxen were plowing, and the donkeys were feeding beside them,
and the Sabeans attacked them, and took them away, and they killed the servants with the edge of the sword, and only I alone have escaped to tell you.”
While he was still speaking, another came and said, “The fire of God fell from heaven and burned up the sheep and the servants and consumed them, and I alone have escaped to tell you.”

While he was still speaking, another came and said, “The Chaldeans formed three companies and made a raid on the camels and have taken them away. They killed the servants with the edge of the sword, and I alone have escaped to tell you.”
While he was still speaking, another came and said, “Your sons and your daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother’s house,
and behold, a great wind came from the wilderness and struck the four corners of the house, and it fell on the young people, and they are dead; and I alone have escaped to tell you.”
Then Job stood up, tore his robe, and shaved his head. He fell to the ground and worshipped.
He said,
In all this Job did not sin, and he did not accuse God of wrongdoing.
Again there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord, and the Adversary came also among them to present himself before the Lord.
The Lord said to the Adversary, “From where do you come?”

The Lord said to the Adversary, “Have you considered My servant Job, that there is none like him on the earth, a blameless and an upright man, who fears God and avoids evil? He still holds fast his integrity, although you moved Me against him, to destroy him without cause.”
The Adversary answered the Lord, saying, “Skin for skin; yes, all that a man has he will give for his life.
Put forth Your hand now and touch his bone and his flesh, and he will curse You to Your face.”
The Lord said to the Adversary, “Very well, he is in your hand, but spare his life.”
Therefore, the Adversary went out from the presence of the Lord, and he afflicted Job with severe sores from the sole of his foot to the top of his head.
So he took a piece of broken pottery with which to scrape himself while he was sitting among the ashes.
His wife said to him, “Are you still maintaining your integrity? Curse God and die.”
He said to her, “You talk like one of the foolish women talks. Will we indeed accept the good from God but not accept the adversity?”

Three friends of Job heard about all this evil that had come upon him, and each one came from his own place: Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite. They had agreed together to come to mourn with him and to comfort him.
They saw him from a distance and did not recognize him, so they wept aloud. Each one tore his robe, and they tossed dust into the air above their heads.
Then they sat down with him on the ground seven days and seven nights. Meanwhile, no one was speaking to him at all because they saw that his pain was severe.
After this Job opened his mouth, and cursed the day of his birth.
Job said:
“Let the day perish in which I was born
As for that day, let it be darkness;
Let darkness and the shadow of death claim it;
As for that night, let darkness capture it;
Yes, as for that night, let it be barren!
Let them curse it who curse any day,
Let its morning stars be dark;
because it did not shut the doors of my mother’s womb,
“Why did I not die at birth?
Why did her knees receive me?
For now I would be lying down and would be at peace;
with kings and counselors of the earth,
or with princes who had gold,
Or why was I not hidden like a stillborn child,
There the wicked will have stopped causing trouble,
Captives will relax together;
The small and great, they are there,
“Why is light given to the miserable,
who look for death, but it is not there;
who rejoice exceedingly,
And why is light given to a man
For my sighing comes before I eat,
For the thing which I greatly feared has happened to me,
I am not at peace; I have no quiet,
Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered:
“If one attempts a word with you, will you be impatient?
Surely you have instructed many,
Your words have raised up him who was falling,
But now it comes upon you, and you are weary;
Is not your reverence your confidence?
“Remember now, who being innocent ever perished?
Just like I have seen, those who plow iniquity
By the breath of God they perish,
The roaring of the lion, and the voice of the fierce lion,
The old lion perishes for lack of prey,
“Now a word was brought to me secretly,
Amid disquieting thoughts from night visions,
terror and trembling came to me,
A breath of wind was passing before my face,
It stood still,
‘Can a mortal be more righteous than God?
He does not trust in His servants,
Even more, those who dwell in houses of clay,
They are broken in pieces from morning to evening;
Are not their tent ropes plucked up,
“Call out now; is anyone answering you?
For anger slays the foolish man,
Yes, I saw the foolish taking root,
May his children be far from safety,
whose harvest the hungry eats up,
For affliction does not come out of the dust,
but man is born to trouble,
“Indeed, I would appeal to God,
who does the great and the inscrutable,
He gives rain on the surface of the earth
He sets on high those who are lowly,
He frustrates the schemes of the crafty,
He catches the wise in their own craftiness,
In the daytime they encounter darkness,
But the needy He saves from the sword,
So the helpless has hope,
“Behold, blessed is the man whom God corrects!
for He wounds, but He applies the bandage;
In six crises He will deliver you;
In famine He will redeem you from death,
You will be hidden from the lash of the tongue,
You will laugh at devastation and famine,
For you will have a covenant with the stones of the field,
You will know that your tent is peaceful,
You will know that your offspring will be many
You go to the grave in a full age,
“Behold, we have investigated all this, and it is so;
But Job answered:
“Oh, that my grief were fully weighed,
For now it would be heavier than the sand of the sea;
For the arrows of the Almighty are within me;
Does the wild donkey bray when he has grass?
Is tasteless food eaten without salt?
My soul refuses to touch them;
“Oh, that I might have my request,
That it would please God to crush me,
Then I would still have comfort;
“What strength do I have, that I should hope?
Is my strength the strength of stones?
Is there no help within me?
“A despairing man should be shown kindness from his friend,
My brothers have acted deceitfully like a riverbed,
which are dark because of the ice,
In time they are scorched; they vanish!
The caravans of their way turn aside;
The caravans of Tema looked,
They were disappointed because they were confident;
For now you are nothing;
Did I say, ‘Give to me’?
Or, ‘Deliver me from the power of the enemy’?
“Teach me, and I will hold my tongue,
How forceful are right words!
Do you mean to correct my words,
Yes, you cast lots for the fatherless,
“And now, please give me your attention,
Turn, I pray, let there be no injustice!
Is there injustice on my tongue?
“Is there not a time of hard service for a man upon earth?
Like a servant, he longs for the shade,
so I have been assigned months of futility,
When I lie down, I say,
My flesh is covered with worms and caked with dirt;
“My days fly more swiftly than a weaver’s shuttle,
Oh, remember that my life is a breath!
The eye of him who sees me will behold me no more;
As the cloud disappears and vanishes away,
He will never return to his house,
“Therefore, I will not restrain my mouth;
Am I the sea, or a sea monster,
When I say, ‘My bed will comfort me,
then You scare me with dreams
so that my soul chooses strangling,
I loathe my life; I would not live forever;
“What is man, that You should exalt him,
and that You should visit him every morning,
How long until You look away from me?
Have I sinned? What am I doing to You,
And why do You not pardon my transgression
Then Bildad the Shuhite answered:
“How long will you speak these things,
Does God pervert judgment?
If your children sinned against Him,
If you yourself would seek God earnestly,
if you were pure and upright,
Though your beginning was small,
“Please, ask the former generation,
for we were born but yesterday and know nothing,
Will they not teach you, and tell you,
Can the papyrus grow up without a marsh?
While it is yet green and not cut down,
So are the paths of all who forget God;
whose confidence will be cut off,
He will lean upon his house, but it will not stand;
He is green before the sun,
His roots are wrapped around the rock heap,
If he is uprooted from his place,
Behold, this is the joy of his way,
“Surely, God will not cast away a perfect man,
until He fills your mouth with laughing,
Those who hate you will be clothed with shame,
Then Job answered:
“Truly, I know it is so,
If one would dispute with Him,
He is wise in heart and mighty in strength.
He who removes mountains, and they know not,
He who shakes the earth out of its place,
He who commands the sun, and it does not rise;
He who alone spreads out the heavens,
He who makes the Bear, Orion, and Pleiades,
He who does great things, beyond discovery,
Yes, He would cross before me, and I would not see Him;
Yes, He takes away; who can hinder Him?
God will not withdraw His anger.
“How, then, can I myself answer Him,
Even if I were righteous I could not answer;
If I called, and He answered me,
For He crushes me with a storm
He will not allow me to get my breath,
If it is a matter of strength, indeed, He is strong;
Though I were righteous, my own mouth would condemn me;
“Though I were perfect,
It is all one thing; therefore I said,
If the whip kills suddenly,
The earth is given into the hand of the wicked.
“Now my days are swifter than a runner;
They pass by like reed skiffs,
If I say, ‘I will forget my complaint;
I am afraid of all my sorrows;
If I am guilty,
If I wash myself with snow water
yet You will plunge me into the pit,
“For He is not a man as I am, that I should answer Him,
Nor is there a mediator between us,
Let Him take His rod away from me,
Then I would speak and not fear Him,
“My soul loathes my life;
I will say to God, Do not condemn me;
Is it good for You that You should oppress,
Do You have eyes of flesh?
Are Your days as the days of man?
that You inquire after my iniquity
You know that I am not wicked,
“Your hands have shaped me and made me completely,
Remember, I pray,
Have You not poured me out as milk
You have clothed me with skin and flesh,
You have granted me life and loyal love,
“These things You have hidden in Your heart.
If I have sinned, then You would watch me,
If I am wicked, woe unto me;
For if my head is lifted up, You would hunt me like a lion,
You renew Your witnesses against me
“Why then did You bring me forth out of the womb?
I should have been as though I had not been;
Are not my days few? Stop then,
before I go and do not return,
a land of darkness, as darkness itself;
Then Zophar the Naamathite answered:
“Should not the multitude of words be answered?
Should your empty talk make men hold their peace?
For you have said, ‘My teaching is pure,
But oh, that God would speak
and that He would show you the secrets of wisdom!
“Can you search out the deep things of God?
It is as high as heaven; what can you do?
Its measure is longer than the earth
“If He passes through, and imprisons, and gathers together for judgment,
For He knows worthless men;
For an empty-headed man will become wise,
“If you prepare your heart
if iniquity is in your hand, put it far away,
for then you will lift up your face without blemish;
because you will forget misery,
and your life will be brighter than noonday,
You will trust because there is hope;
Also you will lie down, and none will make you afraid;
But the eyes of the wicked will fail,
And Job answered:
“No doubt but you are the people,
But I have understanding as well as you;
“I am a laughingstock to my neighbor,
He whose foot is unsteady
The tents of robbers are at peace,
“But now ask the beasts, and let them teach you;
or speak to the earth, let it teach you;
Who among all these does not know
in whose hand is the soul of every living thing
Does not the ear test words
Wisdom is with the elderly,
“With Him are wisdom and strength;
Surely, He tears down, and it cannot be built again;
Surely, He withholds the waters, and they dry up;
With Him are strength and wisdom.
He leads counselors away stripped
He has loosened the bonds imposed by kings
He leads away priests stripped
He removes speech from the trusted ones
He pours contempt upon princes
He uncovers deep things out of darkness
He increases the nations and destroys them;
He takes away the understanding of the chiefs of the people of the earth,
They grope in the dark without light,
“Behold, my eye has seen all this;
What you know, I also know the same;
Surely I would speak to the Almighty,
But you are plasterers of falsehood;
Oh, that you would altogether hold your peace,
Hear now my reasoning,
Will you speak wickedly for God?
Will you take His side?
Is it good that He would search you out?
He will surely rebuke you,
Will not His excellence make you afraid,
Your reminders are parables made of ashes;
“Hold your peace; leave me alone, that I may speak,
Why do I take my flesh in my teeth
Though He slay me, yet will I trust in Him,
He also will be my salvation,
Listen carefully to my speech,
Behold, I have prepared my case;
Who is he who will plead with me?
“Only grant me two things,
Withdraw Your hand far from me,
Then call, and I will answer;
How many are my iniquities and sins?
Why do You hide Your face
Will You frighten a leaf driven to and fro?
For You write bitter things against me
You put my feet in the stocks
“Man, as a rotten thing, decays,
“Man who is born of a woman
He comes forth like a flower and withers;
Do You open Your eyes on such a one,
Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean?
Seeing his days are determined,
turn from him, that he may rest,
“For there is hope for a tree,
Though its root may grow old in the earth,
yet at the scent of water it will bud
But man dies and wastes away;
As the waters disappear from the sea,
so man lies down and does not rise;
“Oh, that You would hide me in the grave,
If a man dies, will he live again?
You will call, and I will answer You;
For now You number my steps;
My transgression is sealed up in a bag,
“Surely the mountain falling comes to nothing,
The waters wear away the stones;
You prevail forever against him, and he passes on;
His sons come to honor, and he does not know it;
But his flesh on him will have pain,
Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered:
“Should a wise man reply with empty knowledge
Should he reason with unprofitable talk
Yes, you cast off reverence
For your mouth utters your iniquity,
Your own mouth condemns you, and not I;
“Are you the first man who was born?
Have you heard the counsel of God?
What do you know that we do not know?
Both the gray-haired and very aged are among us —
Are the consolations of God too small for you?
Why does your heart carry you away?
that you turn your spirit against God,
“What is man that he should be pure?
Behold, He puts no trust in His holy ones,
How much more abhorred and corrupt is man,
“I will tell you; hear me,
what wise men have told,
to whom alone the land was given,
The wicked man travails with pain all his days,
A dreadful sound is in his ears;
He does not believe that he will return from darkness,
He wanders about for bread, saying, ‘Where is it?’
Trouble and anguish will make him afraid;
For he stretches out his hand against God,
He rushes upon Him, even on His neck,
“He has covered his face with his fatness
He dwells in desolate cities
He will not be rich, nor will his wealth continue,
He will not depart out of darkness;
Let him who is deceived not trust in futility,
It will be accomplished before his time,
He will shake off his unripe grape like the vine,
For the company of hypocrites will be desolate,
They conceive mischief, and give birth to futility;
Then Job answered:
“I have heard many such things;
Will windy words have an end?
I also could speak as you do,
but I would strengthen you with my mouth,
“Though I speak, my grief is not relieved;
But now He has made me weary;
You have filled me with wrinkles, which is a witness against me;
He has torn me in His wrath, and He has carried a grudge against me.
They have gaped upon me with their mouth;
God has delivered me to the ungodly
I was at ease, but He has shattered me.
His archers surround me;
He pierces me with thrust after thrust;
“I have sewn sackcloth over my skin
My face is inflamed with weeping,
though not for any violence in my hands,
“O earth, do not cover my blood,
Even now, behold, my witness is in heaven,
My friends scorn me;
Oh, that one might plead for a man with God,
“For when a few years have passed,
“My spirit is broken,
Are not mockers with me?
“Now put down a pledge for me with Yourself.
For You have hidden their heart from understanding.
He who speaks flattery to his friends,
“And He has made me a byword of the people,
My eye also is dim because of sorrow,
Upright men will be astonished at this,
The righteous also will hold to his way,
“But as for you all, return and come now,
My days are past, my purposes are broken off,
They change the night into day;
If I wait, the grave is my house;
I have said to the pit, ‘You are my father’;
Where now is my hope?
Will they go down to the gates of Sheol?
Then Bildad the Shuhite answered:
“How long will it be until you put an end to words?
Why are we counted as beasts
You who tear yourself in anger,
“Yes, the light of the wicked will be put out,
The light will be dark in his tent,
The steps of his strength will be shortened,
For he is cast into a net by his own feet,
The trap will take him by the heel,
The snare is laid for him in the ground,
Terrors will make him afraid on every side
His strength will be hungry,
It will devour the parts of his skin;
His confidence will be rooted out of his tent,
They dwell in his tent who have no part with him;
His roots will be dried up beneath,
The memory of him will perish from the earth,
He will be driven from light into darkness,
He has neither descendant nor posterity among his people,
They who come after him will be astonished at his day,
Surely such are the dwellings of the wicked,
Then Job answered:
“How long will you torment my soul
These ten times you have reproached me;
And if indeed I have erred,
If indeed you exalt yourselves against me
know now that God has bent me
“Behold, I cry out concerning wrong, but I am not heard;
He has fenced up my way that I cannot pass,
He has stripped me of my glory
He has destroyed me on every side, and I am gone;
He has also kindled His wrath against me,
His troops come together
“He has removed my brothers far from me,
My relatives have failed,
Those who dwell in my house, and my maidservants,
I called my servant, but he gave me no answer;
My breath is offensive to my wife;
Yes, young children despise me;
All my close friends abhorred me,
My bones cling to my skin and to my flesh,
“Have pity upon me, have pity upon me, O you my friends,
Why do you persecute me as God does,
“Oh, that my words were written!
That they were engraved with an iron pen
For I know that my Redeemer lives,
and after my skin is destroyed,
whom I will see for myself,
“If you should say, ‘How shall we persecute him?’
be afraid of the sword for yourselves;
Then Zophar the Naamathite answered:
“Therefore my thoughts cause me to answer,
I have heard the rebuke that disgraces me,
“Do you not know this of old,
that the triumphing of the wicked is short,
Though his loftiness extends to the heavens,
yet he will perish forever like his own excrement;
He will fly away like a dream and will not be found;
The eye that saw him will see him no more;
His children will seek favor from the poor,
His bones are full of his youthful vigor,
“Though evil is sweet in his mouth,
though he spares it and does not forsake it,
yet his food in his stomach turns sour;
He has swallowed down riches,
He will suck the poison of cobras;
He will not see the streams, the rivers,
He will give back the produce of labor and will not swallow it down.
because he has oppressed and has forsaken the poor.
“Because he knows no quietness in his belly,
Nothing is left for him to eat;
In his self-sufficiency he will be in distress;
When he is about to fill his belly,
He will flee from the iron weapon;
It is drawn and comes out of the body;
Total darkness is stored up for his treasures.
The heavens will reveal his iniquity,
The increase of his house will depart,
This is the wicked man’s portion from God,
But Job answered:
“Listen carefully to my speech,
Bear with me that I may speak,
“As for me, is my complaint against man?
Look at me and be astonished,
Even when I remember I am afraid,
Why do the wicked live and become old;
Their descendants are established with them in their sight,
Their houses are safe from fear,
Their bull breeds without failure;
They send forth their little ones like a flock,
They take up the tambourine and harp
They spend their days in wealth,
Therefore they say to God, ‘Depart from us,
Who is the Almighty, that we should serve Him?
Indeed, their prosperity is not in their hand.
“How often is the lamp of the wicked put out?
They are like straw before the wind,
God stores up their iniquity for their children;
Let their eyes see their own destruction,
For what do they care about their households after them,
“Can anyone teach God knowledge,
One dies in his full strength,
His pails are full of milk,
Another dies in the bitterness of his soul,
They will lie down alike in the dust,
“Behold, I know your thoughts,
For you say, ‘Where is the house of the prince?
Have you not asked them who travel the road?
For the wicked are reserved for the day of destruction;
Who will declare his way to his face?
Yet will he be brought to the grave
The clods of the valley will be sweet unto him;
“How then can you comfort me with emptiness,
Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered:
“Can a man be profitable to God,
Is it any pleasure to the Almighty that you are righteous?
“Is it because of your fear of Him that He corrects you,
Is not your wickedness great,
For you have taken a pledge from your brother for nothing,
You have not given water to the weary to drink,
But as for the mighty man, he possessed the earth,
You have sent widows away empty,
Therefore snares are all around you,
or darkness, so that you cannot see;
“Is not God in the height of heaven?
And you say, ‘What does God know?
Thick clouds are His covering, so He cannot see;
Will you keep to the old way,
They were cut down before their time;
They said to God, ‘Depart from us,’
Yet He filled their houses with good things;
“The righteous see it and are glad,
‘Surely our adversaries are cut down,
“Now acquaint yourself with Him and be at peace;
Receive, I pray, the teaching from His mouth,
If you return to the Almighty, you will be built up;
Then you will lay up gold as dust,
Yes, the Almighty will be your gold
for then you will delight yourself in the Almighty,
You will make your prayer to Him, and He will hear you,
You will also declare a matter, and it will be established unto you;
When men are cast down, and you say, ‘There is a time of exaltation!’
He will even deliver one who is not innocent;
Then Job answered:
“Today also my complaint is bitter;
Oh, that I knew where I might find Him,
I would present my case before Him
I would know the words that He would answer me
Will He plead against me with His great power?
There the righteous might dispute with Him;
“Behold, I go forward, but He is not there,
when He works on the left hand, I cannot behold Him;
But He knows the way that I take;
My foot has held fast to His steps;
I have not departed from the commandment of His lips;
“But He is resolute, and who can turn Him?
For He performs what is appointed for me,
Therefore I am troubled at His presence;
For God makes my heart soft,
because I was not cut off from the presence of darkness,
“Since times of judgment are not kept by the Almighty,
Some remove the landmarks;
They drive away the donkey of the orphan;
They turn away the needy;
Behold, as wild donkeys in the desert,
They gather their fodder in the field,
They cause the naked to lodge without clothing,
They are wet with the showers of the mountains
They snatch the fatherless from the breast
They cause him to go naked without clothing,
They press out oil within their walls
Men groan from outside the city,
“They are those who rebel against the light;
The murderer, rising with the light, kills the poor and needy,
Also the eye of the adulterer waits for the twilight,
In the dark they break into houses,
For the morning is the same to them as the shadow of death;
“He is swift as the waters.
Drought and heat consume the snow waters;
The womb will forget him;
He preys on the barren who do not bear,
But God draws the mighty away with His power;
He gives them security, and they rely on it;
They are exalted for a little while but are gone and brought low;
“If it is not so, who will prove me a liar
Then Bildad the Shuhite answered:
“Dominion and fear are with Him;
Is there any number to His armies?
How then can man be righteous with God?
Behold, even the moon does not shine,
how much less man, who is a maggot?
But Job answered:
“How have you helped him who is without power?
How have you counseled him who has no wisdom?
To whom have you uttered words?
“The departed spirits tremble under the waters,
The underworld is naked before Him,
He stretches out the north over empty space,
He binds up the waters in His thick clouds,
He covers the face of the full moon
He has circled the waters with boundaries,
The pillars of heaven tremble
He divides the sea with His power,
By His breath He has made fair the heavens;
Indeed, these are but a part of His ways,
Moreover Job continued his discourse:
“As God lives, who has taken away my judgment,
all the while my spirit is in me,
my lips will not speak wickedness,
God forbid that I should justify you.
My righteousness I hold fast and will not let it go;
“Let my enemy be like the wicked,
For what is the hope of the hypocrite,
Will God hear his cry
Will he delight himself in the Almighty?
“I will teach you about the hand of God;
Behold, all of you have seen it;
“This is the portion of a wicked man with God,
If his children are multiplied, it is for the sword,
Those who survive him will be buried in death,
Though he heaps up silver like the dust
he may pile it up, but the just will wear it,
He builds his house like a moth,
The rich man will lie down, but he will not be gathered;
Terrors overtake him like floodwaters;
The east wind carries him away, and he departs;
For God will cast it upon him and not spare;
Men will clap their hands at him
“Surely there is a mine for the silver,
Iron is taken out of the earth,
Man puts an end to darkness,
He breaks open a shaft away from the inhabitants;
As for the earth, from it comes bread,
Its stones are the source of sapphires,
There is a path that no bird knows,
the lion cubs have not trodden it,
He puts forth his hand upon the rock;
He cuts out rivers among the rocks,
He prevents the floods from overflowing,
“But where will wisdom be found?
Man does not know its price,
The depth says, ‘It is not in me,’
It cannot be bought for gold,
It cannot be valued in the gold of Ophir,
The gold and the crystal cannot equal it,
No mention will be made of coral or of pearls,
The topaz of Cush will not equal it,
“From where then does wisdom come?
It is hidden from the eyes of all living
Destruction and Death say,
God understands its way,
For He looks to the ends of the earth,
to make the weight of the wind,
When He made a decree for the rain,
then He saw it and declared it;
To man He said:
Moreover Job continued his discourse:
“Oh, that I were as in months past,
when His lamp shone upon my head,
as I was in the days of my autumn youth,
when the Almighty was still with me,
when my steps were bathed in butter,
“When I went out to the gate of the city,
the young men saw me and hid themselves,
The princes refrained from talking,
The nobles held their peace,
When the ear heard, then it blessed me;
because I delivered the poor who cried,
The blessing of the perishing man came upon me,
I put on righteousness, and it clothed me;
I was eyes for the blind,
I was a father to the poor,
I broke the jaws of the wicked
“Then I said, ‘I will die in my nest,
My root was spread out by the waters,
My glory was fresh in me,
“Men listened to me and waited,
After my words they did not speak again,
They waited for me as for the rain,
If I mocked at them, they did not believe it,
I chose the way for them and sat as chief,
“But now those who are younger than I mock me,
Yes, how does the strength of their hands profit me?
For want and famine
Who pluck mallow by the bushes,
They were driven out from among men;
They had to dwell in the rocky riverbeds,
Among the bushes they brayed;
They were children of fools, yes, children of vile men;
“Now I am their taunting song;
They abhor me, they flee far from me;
Because He has loosed my bowstring and afflicted me,
At my right hand their brood arises;
They tear apart my path,
They came upon me as a wide breach, with a crash they came;
Terrors are turned on me;
“Now my soul is poured out within me;
My bones are pierced in me at night,
By the great force of my disease my garment is changed;
He has cast me into the mire,
“I cry unto You, but You do not hear me;
You have become cruel to me;
You lift me up to the wind and cause me to ride on it;
For I know that You will bring me to death,
“Surely He will not stretch out His hand to the grave,
Did I not weep for him who was in trouble?
When I looked for good, then evil disaster came upon me;
My insides boiled and did not rest;
I went mourning without the sun;
I am a brother of jackals
My skin is black upon me,
My harp is turned to mourning,
“I made a covenant with my eyes;
For what portion of God is there from above?
Does not destruction belong to the wicked,
Does He not see my ways,
“If I have walked in vanity,
let me be weighed in an even balance
If my step has turned out of the path,
then let me sow, but let another eat;
“If my heart has been deceived by a woman,
then let my wife grind for another,
For this is a heinous crime;
For it is a fire that consumes to destruction
“If I have despised the cause of my male or female servant
what then will I do when God rises up?
Did not He who made me in the womb make him?
“If I have kept the poor from their desire,
or have eaten my morsel by myself,
(but from my youth he was brought up with me, as with a father,
if I have seen anyone perish for lack of clothing,
if his body has not blessed me,
if I have lifted up my hand against the fatherless,
then let my arm fall from my shoulder blade,
For destruction from God is a terror to me,
“If I have made gold my hope,
if I rejoiced because my wealth was great,
if I saw the sun when it shined,
and my heart has been secretly enticed,
this also would be an iniquity to be punished by the judge,
“If I rejoiced at the destruction of him who hated me,
(nor have I allowed my mouth to sin
if the men of my tent have not said,
(the stranger has not lodged in the street,
if I covered my transgressions as any man,
did I fear a great multitude,
“Oh, that one would hear me!
Surely I would carry it on my shoulder
I would declare to Him the number of my steps;
“If my land cries out against me,
if I have eaten its fruit without money,
let thistles grow instead of wheat,
So these three men ceased answering Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.
Then the wrath of Elihu the son of Barakel the Buzite, of the family of Ram, was aroused; his wrath was aroused against Job because he justified himself rather than God.
His wrath was aroused also against his three friends because they had found no answer and yet had condemned Job.
Now Elihu had waited until Job had spoken because they were older than he.
When Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of these three men, then his wrath was aroused.
Elihu the son of Barakel the Buzite answered:
I said, ‘Age should speak,
But there is a spirit in man,
Great men are not always wise,
“Therefore I say,
Indeed, I waited for your words;
Yes, I paid attention to you;
Lest you say, ‘We have found wisdom’;
Now he has not directed his words against me,
“They are amazed; they answer no more;

And so it was, that after the Lord had spoken these words to Job, the Lord said to Eliphaz the Temanite, “My wrath is kindled against you and against your two friends, for you have not spoken of Me what is right as My servant Job has.

And now, take for yourselves seven bulls and seven rams, and go to My servant Job, and offer up for yourselves a burnt offering; and My servant Job will pray for you. For him I will accept, lest I deal with you according to your folly, in that you have not spoken of Me the thing which is right like My servant Job.”
So Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite went and did as the Lord had commanded them; the Lord also accepted Job.
And the Lord restored the fortunes of Job when he prayed for his friends, and also the Lord gave Job twice as much as he had before.

Then all of his brothers, and all his sisters, and all of those who had been of acquaintance before came to Job, and they ate bread with him in his house, and they consoled him and comforted him for all the adversity that the Lord had brought upon him. Every man also gave him a piece of money and an earring of gold.
So the Lord blessed the latter days of Job more than his beginning, for he had fourteen thousand sheep, and six thousand camels, and one thousand yoke of oxen, and one thousand female donkeys.
He had also seven sons and three daughters.
He called the name of the first Jemimah; and the name of the second Keziah; and the name of the third Keren-Happuch.
In all the land, there were no women as beautiful as the daughters of Job, and their father gave them an inheritance along with their brothers.
After this, Job lived one hundred and forty years, and saw his sons, and their sons to the fourth generation.
So Job died, being old and full of days.

I, Qoheleth, have been king over Israel in Jerusalem.
I set my heart to seek and to investigate with wisdom everything that is done under heaven. It is a burdensome task that God has given to humanity to be occupied with.
I have seen everything that is done under the sun; and behold, everything is vanity and like chasing the wind.
What is bent cannot be straightened,
I spoke in my heart saying, “I have been great and increased in wisdom more than anyone else who has been before me in Jerusalem, and my heart has observed great wisdom and knowledge.”
And I set my heart to know wisdom and to know the folly of ideas, and to know foolish behavior. I know that this as well is like chasing the wind.
For in an abundance of wisdom is an abundance of frustration,
And I said in my heart, “Come, and I will test you with selfish pleasures; enjoy your desires.” And notice that this too is vanity.
And I said of frivolous fun, “They are only senseless ideas,” and regarding selfish pleasure, “What purpose is this?”

I investigated how to cheer up my body with wine, while my heart was still guiding me with wisdom, in order to grasp folly, until I might experience what is good for people to do under heaven during the number of days that they might have life.
I accomplished great works. I built houses for myself and planted vineyards for myself.
I made myself royal gardens and parks, and planted in them all kinds of fruit trees.
I made myself pools of water to irrigate the forests of growing trees.
I even bought male and female slaves, and some were born in my house. I also had a great number of livestock, cattle, and sheep, more than there had been before in Jerusalem.

I also gathered for myself silver and gold and precious possessions of kings and provinces. I acquired male and female singers, and the sensual delights of any human being, even a harem of many concubines.
I became great and surpassed anyone who had been in Jerusalem before me. Also my wisdom remained with me.
Everything my eyes wanted, I did not refuse them.

So I began to hate life, because the labor that was done under the sun was contemptible to me, for all of this is vanity and a chasing after wind.

So I turned to give my heart up to despair concerning all the toil of my labors under the sun.
For there is a person who labors with wisdom, knowledge, and skill; yet to a person who did not labor for this, he leaves it as his inheritance. This also is vanity and a great distress.
What becomes a man for all his labor and striving in his heart with which he toils under the sun?
All his days are sorrowful, and his work is a vexation. Even at night his heart finds no rest. This also is vanity.
There is nothing better for a person than to eat and drink, and make his life see the good in his labor. This I have seen is from the hand of God.
For who can even eat or have enjoyment more than I?

To the person who is pleasing before Him, God gives wisdom, knowledge, and joy, but to the one who sins, He gives the task to gather and collect, to give to the other person who is pleasing before God. This also is vanity and a chasing after wind.

I have seen the task that God has given to people to be concerned with.

I know that there is nothing better for people than to be glad and do good in their life,
and also that everyone should eat and drink and experience good in all their labor. This is a gift of God.

For when there is an abundance of dreams and futilities, then words increase too. Therefore it is God you should fear.

There is another vanity that takes place on earth: there are righteous people who are treated according to the deeds of the wicked, and there are wicked people who are treated according to the deeds of the righteous. I observed that this also is vanity.

So I commend enjoyment, because there is nothing better for people under the sun than to eat and drink and enjoy life, for enjoyment will go with a person in his toil all the days of his life that God has given him under the sun.

All this I took to heart, to examine all these matters, how the righteous and the wise and their deeds are in the hand of God. Whether it is love or hate, no person knows everything that will come before these people.

The oxen likewise and the young donkeys that work the ground shall eat cured fodder, which has been winnowed with the shovel and fork.
There shall be on every high mountain and on every high hill rivers and streams of waters in the day of the great slaughter, when the towers fall.

In the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of Assyria came up against all the fortified cities of Judah and took them.
The king of Assyria sent the Rabshakeh from Lachish to Jerusalem to King Hezekiah with a great army. And he stood by the conduit of the upper pool in the highway of the fuller’s field.
Then Eliakim came to him, the son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah, the son of Asaph, the recorder.
The Rabshakeh said to them:
I say, Your counsel and strength for war are only empty words. Now on whom do you rely that you rebel against me?
Behold, you trust in the staff of this broken reed, on Egypt, on which if a man leans, it will go into his hand and pierce it. So is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who rely on him.

But if you say to me, ‘We trust in the Lord our God,’ is it not He whose high places and whose altars Hezekiah has taken away, and said to Judah and to Jerusalem, ‘You shall worship before this altar’?
“Now therefore, come make a bargain with my master the king of Assyria, and I will give you two thousand horses, if you are able on your part to set riders on them.
How then will you turn away one captain of the least of my master’s servants and rely on Egypt for chariots and for horsemen?
Have I now come up without the approval of the Lord against this land to destroy it? The Lord said to me, Go up against this land, and destroy it.”
Then Eliakim and Shebna and Joah said to the Rabshakeh, “Speak now to your servants in Aramaic, for we understand it. And do not speak to us in Hebrew in the ears of the people who are on the wall.”

But the Rabshakeh said, “Has my master sent me only to your master and to you to speak these words? Has he not sent me to the men who sit on the wall, that they may eat their own dung and drink their own urine with you?”
Then the Rabshakeh stood and cried out with a loud voice in Hebrew, and said, “Hear the words of the great king, the king of Assyria.
Thus says the king, ‘Do not let Hezekiah deceive you, for he shall not be able to deliver you;
nor let Hezekiah make you trust in the Lord, saying, The Lord will surely deliver us. This city shall not be delivered into the hand of the king of Assyria.’

“Do not listen to Hezekiah, for thus says the king of Assyria: ‘Make your peace with me and come out to me, and eat every one of his vine and every one of his fig tree, and drink every one the waters of his own cistern,
until I come and take you away to a land like your own land, a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards.
“ ‘Beware lest Hezekiah persuade you, saying, The Lord will deliver us. Has any one of the gods of the nations delivered his land out of the hand of the king of Assyria?
Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim? And when have they delivered Samaria out of my hand?
Who are they among all the gods of these lands that have delivered their land out of my hand, that the Lord should deliver Jerusalem out of my hand?’ ”
But they held their peace, and answered him not a word, for the king’s commandment was, “Do not answer him.”

Then Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah the son of Asaph, the recorder, came to Hezekiah with their clothes torn and told him the words of the Rabshakeh.
When King Hezekiah heard it, he tore his clothes, and covered himself with sackcloth, and went into the house of the Lord.
He sent Eliakim, who was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and the elders of the priests, covered with sackcloth, to Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz.
They said to him, “Thus says Hezekiah: This day is a day of trouble, and of rebuke, and of blasphemy, for children have come to birth, and there is no strength to bring them forth.

Perhaps the Lord your God will hear the words of the Rabshakeh, whom the king of Assyria his master has sent to reproach the living God, and will reprove the words which the Lord your God has heard. Therefore, lift up a prayer for the remnant that is left.”
So the servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah.
Isaiah said to them, “Thus you shall say to your master, ‘Thus says the Lord: Do not be afraid of the words that you have heard, with which the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed Me.
Behold, I will put a spirit in him so that he shall hear a rumor, and return to his own land. And I will cause him to fall by the sword in his own land.’ ”
So the Rabshakeh returned and found the king of Assyria warring against Libnah. For he had heard that the king had left Lachish.
He heard them say concerning Tirhakah king of Cush, “He has come out to make war with you.” And when he heard it, he sent messengers to Hezekiah, saying,
“Thus you shall speak to Hezekiah king of Judah, saying: Do not let your God in whom you trust deceive you, saying, ‘Jerusalem shall not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.’
Behold, you have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all lands by utterly destroying them. So shall you be delivered?
Have the gods of the nations delivered them which my fathers have destroyed, even Gozan and Harran and Rezeph and the sons of Eden who were in Tel-assar?
Where is the king of Hamath, and the king of Arpad, and the kings of the city of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah?”
And Hezekiah received the letter from the hand of the messengers and read it. Then Hezekiah went up to the house of the Lord, and spread it before the Lord.
Hezekiah prayed to the Lord, saying,

Incline Your ear, O Lord, and hear. Open Your eyes, O Lord, and see, and hear all the words of Sennacherib, which he has sent to reproach the living God.

Then the angel of the Lord went out and struck one hundred and eighty-five thousand in the camp of the Assyrians. When others woke up early in the morning, behold, these were all dead bodies.
So Sennacherib king of Assyria departed and returned home and lived in Nineveh.

As he was worshipping in the house of Nisrok, his god, Adrammelek and Sharezer, his sons, struck him with the sword, and they escaped into the land of Ararat. And Esarhaddon his son reigned in his stead.
In those days Hezekiah was mortally ill. And Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, came to him and said to him, “Thus says the Lord: Set your house in order, for you shall die, and not live.”
Then Hezekiah turned his face toward the wall, and prayed to the Lord,
and said, “Remember now, O Lord, I beseech You, how I have walked before You in truth and with a perfect heart, and have done what is good in Your sight.” And Hezekiah wept bitterly.
Then the word of the Lord came to Isaiah, saying:
“Go, and say to Hezekiah, Thus says the Lord, the God of David your father: I have heard your prayer, I have seen your tears. Behold, I will add to your days fifteen years.
I will deliver you and this city out of the hand of the king of Assyria, and I will defend this city.
“This shall be a sign to you from the Lord, that the Lord will do this thing that He has spoken:

Behold, I will cause the shadow on the sundial, which has gone down with the sun on the sundial of Ahaz, to go back ten steps.” So the sun’s shadow returned ten steps on the sundial by which it had gone down.

At that time Marduk-Baladan the son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a present to Hezekiah, for he had heard that he had been sick and had recovered.

Hezekiah was glad and showed them the house of his precious things: the silver, and the gold, and the spices, and the precious ointment, and his whole armory, and all that was found in his treasuries. There was nothing in his house, nor in all his dominion, that Hezekiah did not show them.
Then Isaiah the prophet came to King Hezekiah and said to him, “What did these men say, and from where did they come to you?”
Then he said, “What have they seen in your house?”
Then Isaiah said to Hezekiah, “Hear the word of the Lord of Hosts.

Then Hezekiah said to Isaiah, “The word of the Lord which you have spoken is good.” For he said, “For there shall be peace and truth in my days.”

Whereas you have been forsaken
You shall also suck the milk of the nations

For I, the Lord, love justice,

I will greatly rejoice in the Lord,
For as the earth brings forth her buds,

You shall no more be termed Forsaken,

give Him no rest until He establishes

Oh, that You would rend the heavens and come down,

But we all are as an unclean thing,
There is no one who calls on Your name,
But now, O Lord, You are our Father;
Do not be wrathful beyond measure, O Lord,
Your holy cities are a wilderness;
Our holy and beautiful house where our fathers praised You
Will You refrain Yourself from these things, O Lord?
I was sought by those who did not ask for Me;

a people who provoke Me continually
who sit among the graves
who say, “Stand by yourself; do not come near to me,
Behold, it is written before Me:
your iniquities and the iniquities of your fathers together,

But be glad and rejoice forever

Before they call, I will answer;

Thus says the Lord:

He who kills a bull

Hear the word of the Lord,

As one whom his mother comforts,
Then you shall see this, and your heart shall rejoice,

For by fire and by His sword on all flesh,
Those who sanctify themselves and purify themselves in the gardens behind one tree in the midst, eating swine’s flesh, and abominable things, and mice shall be consumed together, says the Lord.
For I know their works and their thoughts. The time shall come to gather all nations and tongues. And they shall come and see My glory.

I will set a sign among them, and send from them survivors to the nations: to Tarshish, Pul, and Lud —who draw the bow—to Tubal, and Javan, to the coastlands afar off who have not heard My fame or seen My glory. And they shall declare My glory among the nations.

They shall bring all your brothers out of all nations as an offering to the Lord on horses, and in chariots, and in litters, and on mules, and on swift beasts to My holy mountain Jerusalem, says the Lord, as the Israelites bring an offering in a clean vessel into the house of the Lord.
I will also take some of them for priests and for Levites, says the Lord.
For as the new heavens and the new earth which I will make shall remain before Me, says the Lord, so shall your descendants and your name remain.
From one New Moon to another, and from one Sabbath to another, all flesh shall come to worship before Me, says the Lord.

And they shall go forth and look on the corpses of the men who have transgressed against Me. For neither shall their worm die nor shall their fire be quenched. And they shall be an abhorrence to all flesh.
The words of Jeremiah the son of Hilkiah, of the priests who were in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin,
to whom the word of the Lord came in the days of Josiah the son of Amon, king of Judah, in the thirteenth year of his reign.

It came also in the days of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah, to the end of the eleventh year of Zedekiah the son of Josiah, king of Judah, until the captivity of Jerusalem in the fifth month.
Now the word of the Lord came to me, saying,
“Before I formed you in the womb I knew you;
Then I said, “Ah, Lord God! Behold, I cannot speak, for I am a youth.”
But the Lord said to me, “Do not say, ‘I am a youth.’ For you shall go everywhere that I send you, and whatever I command you, you shall speak.
Do not be afraid of their faces, for I am with you to deliver you,” says the Lord.
Then the Lord put forth His hand and touched my mouth. And the Lord said to me, “Behold, I have put My words in your mouth.
Behold, I have this day set you over the nations and over the kingdoms, to root out and to pull down, to destroy and to throw down, to build and to plant.”
Moreover the word of the Lord came to me, saying, “Jeremiah, what do you see?”
Then the Lord said to me, “You have seen well, for I will hasten My word to perform it.”
The word of the Lord came to me the second time, saying, “What do you see?”
Then the Lord said to me: Out of the north calamity will break forth on all the inhabitants of the land.
For behold, I will call all the families of the kingdoms of the north, says the Lord.
I will utter My judgments against them
You therefore gird up your loins and arise, and speak to them all that I command you. Do not be dismayed at their faces, lest I confound you before them.

For behold, I have made you this day a fortified city and an iron pillar and bronze walls against the whole land, against the kings of Judah, against the officials, against the priests, and against the people of the land.
They will fight against you, but they will not prevail against you, for I am with you, says the Lord, to deliver you.
Moreover the word of the Lord came to me, saying,
Go and proclaim in the ears of Jerusalem, saying,
Israel is holy to the Lord,
Hear the word of the Lord, O house of Jacob
Thus says the Lord:
They did not say, “Where is the Lord
And I brought you into a plentiful country
The priests did not say,
Therefore I will yet contend with you,

Has a nation changed their gods,
Be astonished at this, O heavens,
For My people have committed two evils.
Is Israel a servant? Is he a homeborn slave?
The young lions roared at him
Also the men of Memphis and Tahpanhes
Have you not brought this on yourself,
And now what are you doing in the way of Egypt,
Your own wickedness will correct you,
For long ago I have broken your yoke
Yet I had planted you a noble vine,
For though you wash yourself with lye,
How can you say, “I am not polluted,
a wild donkey used to the wilderness
Withhold your foot from being unshod
As the thief is ashamed when he is found,

But where are your gods that you have made for yourself?
Why will you plead with Me?

Can a virgin forget her ornaments,
You prepare your way very well to seek love.
Also in your skirts is found
you say, “I am innocent;

Indeed, you shall go forth from him
If a man divorces his wife,
Lift up your eyes to the high places,
Therefore the showers have been withheld,
Shall you not from this time cry to Me,
Shall He reserve His anger forever?

The Lord said also to me in the days of Josiah the king: Have you seen that which backsliding Israel has done? She has gone up on every high mountain and under every green tree, and there has played the harlot.
I said after she had done all these things, “Turn to Me.” But she did not return. And her treacherous sister Judah saw it.
I saw that for all the adulteries of backsliding Israel, I had put her away and given her a bill of divorce. Yet her treacherous sister Judah did not fear, but went and played the harlot also.
Through the lightness of her harlotry she defiled the land and committed adultery with stones and with trees.
Yet for all this, her treacherous sister Judah has not turned to Me with her whole heart, but feignedly, says the Lord.
The Lord said to me: Backsliding Israel has proved herself more righteous than treacherous Judah.
Go and proclaim these words toward the north, and say:
Only acknowledge your iniquity,
Return, O backsliding sons, says the Lord, for I am married to you. And I will take you, one from a city and two from a family, and I will bring you to Zion.
And I will give you shepherds according to My heart, who shall feed you with knowledge and understanding.

It shall come to pass when you are multiplied and increased in the land in those days, says the Lord, they will say no more, “The ark of the covenant of the Lord.” And it will not come to mind, nor will they remember it, nor will they call for it, nor will it be made any more.

At that time they will call Jerusalem, the Throne of the Lord, and all the nations will be gathered to it, to Jerusalem, for the name of the Lord; nor will they walk any more after the stubbornness of their evil hearts.
In those days the house of Judah will walk with the house of Israel, and they will come together out of the land of the north to the land that I have given to your fathers for an inheritance.
But I said:
Surely as a wife treacherously departs from her husband,
A voice was heard upon the high places,
Return, O backsliding sons,
Truly in vain is salvation hoped for from the hills,
For shame has devoured the labor
We lie down in our shame,
If you will return, O Israel,
You shall swear, “As the Lord lives,”
For thus says the Lord to the men of Judah and Jerusalem:
Circumcise yourselves to the Lord,
Declare in Judah and proclaim in Jerusalem, and say:
Set up the standard toward Zion.
The lion has come up from his thicket,
For this gird yourself with sackcloth,
It shall come to pass in that day, says the Lord,
Then I said, “Ah, Lord God! Surely You have greatly deceived this people and Jerusalem, saying, ‘You shall have peace,’ whereas the sword reaches the throat.”
At that time it will be said to this people and to Jerusalem: A dry wind of the high places in the wilderness toward the daughter of My people, not to fan or to cleanse,
even a full wind from those places, will come to Me. Now also I will pronounce judgments against them.
Behold, he shall come up as clouds,
O Jerusalem, wash your heart from wickedness, that you may be saved.
For a voice declares from Dan,
“Report it to the nations, now!”
As watchmen of a field, they are against her all around,
Your way and your deeds
My soul, my soul!

“For My people are foolish,
I looked on the earth,

When you are devastated, what will you do?

Run to and fro through the streets of Jerusalem,
Though they say, “The Lord lives,”
O Lord, are not Your eyes upon the truth?
Therefore I said, “Surely these are the poor.

Therefore a lion out of the forest will slay them,

They were as fed horses in the morning;

Go up upon her walls and destroy,

They have lied about the Lord,
And the prophets shall become wind,
Therefore thus says the Lord God of Hosts:

Their quiver is as an open sepulcher,
They will eat up your harvest and your bread
Nevertheless in those days, says the Lord, I will not make a full end of you.

It shall come to pass when they say, “Why does the Lord our God do all these things to us?” then you shall answer them, “As you have forsaken Me and served strange gods in your land, so you will serve strangers in a land that is not yours.”
Declare this in the house of Jacob
Hear this now, O foolish people and without understanding,
Do you not fear Me? says the Lord.
But this people has a revolting and a rebellious heart;
They do not say in their heart,
Your iniquities have turned away these things,
For among My people are found wicked men.
As a cage is full of birds,
They are fat, they are sleek.
Shall I not punish them for these things?

The prophets prophesy falsely,

Therefore I am full of the fury of the Lord;

I have set you as an assayer
They all are stubborn rebels
The bellows blow fiercely,
Men will call them rejected silver,
The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying:
Stand in the gate of the house of the Lord and proclaim there this word:
Thus says the Lord of Hosts, the God of Israel: Amend your ways and your deeds, and I will cause you to dwell in this place.
Do not trust in lying words, saying, “The temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord.”
For if you thoroughly amend your ways and your deeds, if you thoroughly execute justice between a man and his neighbor,
if you do not oppress the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow, and do not shed innocent blood in this place, or walk after other gods to your harm,
then I will cause you to dwell in this place, in the land that I gave to your fathers, forever and ever.
Behold, you trust in lying words that cannot profit.
Shall you steal, murder, and commit adultery, and swear falsely, and burn incense to Baal, and walk after other gods whom you do not know,
and come and stand before Me in this house, which is called by My name, and say, “We are delivered,” so that you may do all these abominations?
Has this house, which is called by My name, become a den of robbers in your eyes? Behold, even I have seen it, says the Lord.
But go now to My place which was in Shiloh, where I set My name at the first, and see what I did to it for the wickedness of My people Israel.
And now, because you have done all these works, says the Lord, and I spoke to you, rising up early and speaking, but you did not hear, and I called you, but you did not answer,
therefore I will do to this house, which is called by My name, in which you trust, and to the place which I gave to you and to your fathers, as I have done to Shiloh.
I will cast you out of My sight as I have cast out all your brothers, even the whole seed of Ephraim.
As for you, do not pray for this people or lift up a cry, or prayer for them, or make intercession to Me, for I will not hear you.
Do you not see what they do in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem?

The children gather wood, and the fathers kindle the fire, and the women knead their dough, to make cakes to the queen of heaven, and to pour out drink offerings to other gods, that they may provoke Me to anger.
Do they provoke Me to anger? says the Lord. Do they not provoke themselves to the shame of their own faces?

Therefore thus says the Lord God: Behold, My anger and My fury will be poured out upon this place, upon man and upon beast, and upon the trees of the field, and upon the fruit of the ground; and it shall burn, and shall not be quenched.
Thus says the Lord of Hosts, the God of Israel: Add your burnt offerings to your sacrifices and eat flesh.
For I spoke not to your fathers, nor commanded them in the day that I brought them out of the land of Egypt, concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices.
But this thing I commanded them, saying, “Obey My voice, and I will be your God, and you shall be My people. And walk in all the ways that I have commanded you, that it may be well with you.”
But they did not listen, nor incline their ear, but walked in the counsels and in the imagination of their evil heart, and went backward and not forward.
Since the day that your fathers came out of the land of Egypt to this day, I have even sent to you all My servants the prophets, daily rising up early and sending them.
Yet they did not listen to Me, nor incline their ear, but hardened their neck. They did worse than their fathers.
Therefore you will speak all these words to them. But they will not listen to you. You will also call to them, but they will not answer you.
You shall say to them: This is a nation that does not obey the voice of the Lord their God or receive correction. Truth has perished, and has been cut off from their mouth.
Cut off your hair, O Jerusalem, and cast it away, and take up a lamentation on high places, for the Lord has rejected and forsaken the generation of His wrath.
For the Judahites have done evil in My sight, says the Lord. They have set their abominations in the house which is called by My name, to pollute it.
They have built the high places of Topheth, which is in the Valley of Ben-hinnom, to burn their sons and their daughters in the fire, which I did not command them, nor did it come into My heart.

Therefore, behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, that it will no more be called Topheth, nor the Valley of Ben-hinnom, but the Valley of Slaughter; for they will bury in Topheth because there is no other place.
The corpses of this people shall be food for the fowl of the heaven and for the beasts of the earth; and no one will frighten them away.

Then I will cause to cease from the cities of Judah and from the streets of Jerusalem the voice of laughter and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride; for the land shall become desolate.

At that time, says the Lord, they will bring out the bones of the kings of Judah, and the bones of his officials, and the bones of the priests, and the bones of the prophets, and the bones of the inhabitants of Jerusalem out of their graves.

And they will spread them before the sun and the moon and all the host of heaven, whom they have loved and whom they have served, and after whom they have walked and whom they have sought, and whom they have worshipped. They will not be gathered or be buried. They will be as dung upon the face of the earth.
Death will be chosen rather than life by all the rest of those who remain of this evil family, which remains in all the places wherever I have driven them, says the Lord of Hosts.
Moreover you shall say to them, Thus says the Lord:
Why then is this people of Jerusalem
I listened and heard,
Indeed, the stork in the sky
How do you say, “We are wise,
The wise men are ashamed;
Therefore I will give their wives to others,
For they have healed the brokenness
Were they ashamed when they had committed abomination?
I will surely consume them,
Why do we sit still?
We looked for peace,
The snorting of his horses
Behold, I will send serpents against you,
My sorrow is beyond healing;
Behold, the cry of the daughter of my people
“The harvest is past,
For the brokenness of the daughter of my people am I broken;
Is there no balm in Gilead?
Oh, that my head were waters
Oh, that I had in the wilderness
They bend their tongues like their bow;
Let everyone be on guard against his neighbor,
Everyone deceives his neighbor
Your habitation is in the midst of deceit;
Therefore thus says the Lord of Hosts:
Their tongue is a deadly arrow;
Shall I not punish them for these things?
For the mountains I will take up a weeping and wailing,
I will make Jerusalem a heap of ruins

Who is the wise man who may understand this? And who is he to whom the mouth of the Lord has spoken, that he may declare it? Why is the land ruined and burned up like a wilderness, so that no one passes through?
And the Lord said: Because they have forsaken My law which I set before them, and have not obeyed My voice, nor walked in it,
but have walked after the imagination of their own heart and after the Baals, which their fathers taught them.
Therefore thus says the Lord of Hosts, the God of Israel: Behold, I will feed them, even this people, with wormwood and give them water of gall to drink.
I will scatter them also among the nations, whom neither they nor their fathers have known. And I will send a sword after them until I have consumed them.
Thus says the Lord of Hosts:
And let them make haste
For a voice of wailing is heard out of Zion,
Yet hear the word of the Lord, O you women,
“For death has come up into our windows;
Speak, Thus says the Lord:
Thus says the Lord:
but let him who glories glory in this,
Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, that I will punish all who are circumcised and yet uncircumcised —

Egypt, Judah, Edom, the Ammonites, Moab, and all who dwell in the wilderness who clip the hair on their temples, for all these nations are uncircumcised, and all the house of Israel are uncircumcised of heart.
Hear the word which the Lord speaks to you, O house of Israel.
Thus says the Lord:
For the customs of the people are vain;
They deck it with silver and with gold;
They are as a scarecrow in a cucumber field,
There is no one like You, O Lord.
Who would not fear You,
But they are altogether unthinking and foolish;
Silver spread into plates is brought from Tarshish,
But the Lord is the true God;
Thus you shall say to them: The gods that have not made the heavens and the earth, even they shall perish from the earth and from under these heavens.
He has made the earth by His power.
When He utters His voice, there is a multitude of waters in the heavens,
Every man is stupid, without knowledge;
They are vain and a work of mockery;
The portion of Jacob is not like them,
Gather up your wares out of the land,
For thus says the Lord:
Woe is me because of my brokenness!
My tabernacle is devastated,
For the shepherds have become unthinking
Behold, the sound of the report has come,
O Lord, I know that the way of man is not in himself;
O Lord, correct me, but with justice,
Pour out Your fury upon the nations
The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying:
Hear the words of this covenant, and speak to the men of Judah and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
And say you to them, Thus says the Lord God of Israel: Cursed is the man who does not obey the words of this covenant,

which I commanded your fathers in the day that I brought them out of the land of Egypt, from the iron furnace, saying, Obey My voice, and do according to all which I command you. So you shall be My people, and I will be your God,
that I may perform the oath which I have sworn to your fathers, to give them a land flowing with milk and honey, as it is this day.
Then the Lord said to me: Proclaim all these words in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem: saying, Hear the words of this covenant, and do them.
For I earnestly warned your fathers in the day that I brought them up out of the land of Egypt, even to this day, rising early and warning, saying, Obey My voice.

Yet they did not obey or incline their ear, but everyone walked in the imagination of their evil heart. Therefore I will bring upon them all the words of this covenant, which I commanded them to do, but which they did not do.
The Lord said to me: A conspiracy has been found among the men of Judah and among the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

They have turned back to the iniquities of their forefathers who refused to hear My words. And they have gone after other gods to serve them. The house of Israel and the house of Judah have broken My covenant which I made with their fathers.
Therefore thus says the Lord, behold, I will bring calamity upon them which they will not be able to escape. And though they cry to Me, I will not listen to them.
Then the cities of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem will go and cry to the gods to whom they offer incense. But they will not save them at all in the time of their trouble.

For according to the number of your cities are your gods, O Judah. And according to the number of the streets of Jerusalem you have set up altars to that shameful thing, even altars to burn incense to Baal.
Therefore do not pray for this people, nor lift up a cry or prayer for them. For I will not hear them in the time that they cry to Me because of their trouble.
What right has My beloved in My house,
The Lord called your name,

For the Lord of Hosts, who planted you, has pronounced disaster against you, because of the evil of the house of Israel and of the house of Judah, which they have done against themselves to provoke Me to anger in offering incense to Baal.
The Lord has made it known to me and I knew it; then You showed me their deeds.
But I was like a gentle lamb that is brought to the slaughter, and I did not know that they had devised plots against me, saying,
But, O Lord of Hosts, who judges righteously,
Therefore thus says the Lord of the men of Anathoth who seek your life, saying, “Do not prophesy in the name of the Lord so that you not die by our hand.”
Therefore thus says the Lord of Hosts: Behold, I will punish them. The young men shall die by the sword. Their sons and their daughters shall die by famine.
And there shall be no remnant of them, for I will bring calamity upon the men of Anathoth, even the year of their punishment.
Righteous are You, O Lord,
You have planted them; indeed, they have taken root;
But You, O Lord, know me;
How long shall the land mourn
If you have run with the footmen,
For even your brothers and the household of your father,
I have forsaken My house,
My inheritance is to Me
My inheritance is to Me
Many shepherds have destroyed My vineyard;
They have made it desolate,
The destroyers have come
They have sown wheat, but reap thorns;

Thus says the Lord: Against all My evil neighbors who touch the inheritance which I have caused My people Israel to inherit, behold, I will pluck them out of their land and pluck out the house of Judah from among them.
It shall come to pass that after I have plucked them out, I will again have compassion on them, and will bring them back, every man to his inheritance, and every man to his land.

It shall come to pass if they will diligently learn the ways of My people, to swear by My name, “As the Lord lives,” as they taught My people to swear by Baal, then they will be built up in the midst of My people.
But if they will not obey, I will utterly pluck up and destroy that nation, says the Lord.
Thus says the Lord to me, “Go and buy yourself a linen waistband and put it upon your loins, and do not put it in water.”
So I bought a waistband according to the word of the Lord and put it on my loins.
The word of the Lord came to me the second time, saying,
“Take the waistband that you have, which is upon your loins, and arise, go to the Euphrates and hide it there in a hole of the rock.”
So I went and hid it by the Euphrates, as the Lord had commanded me.
After many days the Lord said to me, “Arise, go to the Euphrates and take the waistband from there, which I commanded you to hide there.”
Then I went to the Euphrates, and dug, and took the waistband from the place where I had hidden it. And behold, the waistband was destroyed. It was profitable for nothing.
Then the word of the Lord came to me:
Thus says the Lord: After this manner I will destroy the pride of Judah and the great pride of Jerusalem.

This evil people, who refuse to hear My words, who walk in the imagination of their hearts, and walk after other gods, to serve them, and to worship them, shall be even as this waistband which is good for nothing.

For as the waistband cleaves to the loins of a man, so I have caused the whole house of Israel and the whole house of Judah to cleave to Me, says the Lord, so that they might be to Me a people for renown, and for a praise, and for a glory; but they would not listen.

Therefore you shall speak to them this word: Thus says the Lord God of Israel: Every bottle shall be filled with wine. And when they say to you, “Do we not certainly know that every bottle should be filled with wine?”

then you shall say to them: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I will fill all the inhabitants of this land—even the kings that sit on the throne of David, and the priests, and the prophets, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem—with drunkenness.
I will dash them against one another, even the fathers and the sons together, says the Lord. I will not show pity or spare or have mercy, but will destroy them.
Hear and give heed;
Give glory to the Lord your God,
But if you will not listen to it,
Say to the king and to the queen mother:
The cities of the Negev will be shut up,
Lift up your eyes and see
What will you say when He appoints over you
And if you say in your heart,
Can the Cushite change his skin
Therefore I will scatter them as the stubble
This is your lot,
Therefore I Myself have uncovered your skirts over your face
I have seen your adulteries and your lustful neighings,
The word of the Lord which came to Jeremiah concerning the drought:
Judah mourns,
Their nobles have sent their servants for water;
Because the ground is chapped,
Indeed, the hind also calved in the field
The wild donkeys stand in the high places;
O Lord, though our iniquities testify against us,
O the Hope of Israel,
Why should You be as a man dismayed,
Thus says the Lord to this people:
Then the Lord said to me: Do not pray for the good of this people.

When they fast, I will not hear their cry. And when they offer a burnt offering and a grain offering, I will not accept them. But I will consume them by the sword, and by the famine, and by the pestilence.
Yet I said, “Ah, Lord God! Behold, the prophets say to them, ‘You shall not see the sword nor shall you have famine, but I will give you assured peace in this place.’ ”

Then the Lord said to me: The prophets prophesy lies in My name. I have not sent them, nor have I commanded them, nor have I spoken to them. They prophesy to you a false vision and divination, and emptiness, and the deceit of their heart.

Therefore thus says the Lord concerning the prophets who prophesy in My name though I did not send them, yet they say, “Sword and famine will not be in this land.” By sword and famine those prophets will be consumed.

The people to whom they prophesy will be cast out in the streets of Jerusalem because of the famine and the sword. And they will have no one to bury them, not them, or their wives, or their sons, or their daughters, for I will pour out their wickedness upon them.
Therefore you will say this word to them:
If I go out into the field,
Have You utterly rejected Judah?
We acknowledge, O Lord, our wickedness
Do not abhor us. For Your name’s sake,
Are there any among the idols of the nations that can cause rain?
Then the Lord said to me: Even though Moses and Samuel were to stand before Me, yet My heart would not be with this people. Cast them out of My sight and let them go!
It shall come to pass if they say to you, “Where should we go?” then you shall tell them: Thus says the Lord:
I will appoint over them four kinds of disaster, says the Lord: the sword to slay, the dogs to tear, the birds of the heaven, the beasts of the earth to devour and destroy.
I will cause them to be removed into all kingdoms of the earth, because of Manasseh the son of Hezekiah king of Judah, for that which he did in Jerusalem.
For who shall have pity on you, O Jerusalem?
You who have forsaken Me, says the Lord,
I will winnow them with a winnowing fork
Their widows will increase before Me
She who has borne seven sons languishes;
Woe is me, my mother, that you have borne me
The Lord said:
Can anyone break the northern iron
Your wealth and your treasures
I will make you to pass with your enemies
O Lord, You who know, remember me,
Your words were found and I ate them.
I did not sit in the assembly of mockers,
Why is my pain perpetual
Therefore thus says the Lord:
I will make you to this people
I will deliver you out of the hand of the wicked,
The word of the Lord came also to me, saying:
You shall not take a wife, nor shall you have sons or daughters in this place.

For thus says the Lord concerning the sons and concerning the daughters who are born in this place, and concerning their mothers who bore them, and concerning their fathers who brought them in this land:

They will die of deadly diseases. They will not be lamented, nor shall they be buried. But they will be as dung upon the face of the ground. And they will be consumed by the sword and by famine. And their carcasses will be food for the fowl of heaven and for the beasts of the earth.
For thus says the Lord: Do not enter a house of mourning, or go to lament or bemoan them; for I have taken away My peace from this people, says the Lord, even lovingkindness and mercy.
Both the great and the small will die in this land. They will not be buried; neither will men lament for them, cut themselves, nor make themselves bald for them.
Neither will men tear themselves for them in mourning, to comfort them for the dead; nor will men give them the cup of consolation to drink for their father or for their mother.
Also you shall not go into the house of feasting, to sit with them to eat and to drink.

For thus says the Lord of Hosts, the God of Israel: Behold, I will cause to cease out of this place, before your eyes and in your days, the voice of laughter and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride.

And when you tell this people all these words, and they say to you, “Why has the Lord pronounced all this great disaster against us? Or what is our iniquity? Or what is our sin that we have committed against the Lord our God?”

then you shall say to them: Because your fathers have forsaken Me, says the Lord, and have walked after other gods and have served them and have worshipped them, but have forsaken Me and have not kept My law.
And you have done worse than your fathers, for behold, you each walk after the imaginations of his evil heart, so that they do not listen to Me.
Therefore I will cast you out of this land into a land that you do not know, neither you nor your fathers; and there you will serve other gods day and night because I will not show you favor.
Therefore, behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, that it will no longer be said, “As the Lord lives, who brought up the Israelites out of the land of Egypt,”

but, “As the Lord lives, who brought up the Israelites from the land of the north and from all the lands wherever He had driven them.” And I will bring them again into their land that I gave to their fathers.
